classification.difficultyReason: Find the perpendicular height of an isosceles triangular cross-section using Pythagoras, then calculate prism volume without rounding the intermediate height.

content.prompt: In the diagram below, $ABCFED$ is a right triangular prism, with $AB=AC$.

spec.description: Front triangle ABC and rear triangle DEF, joined by AD, BE and CF. Matching single ticks identify AB and AC. DE, EF and EB are hidden dashed edges. No right-angle mark is present at A. Ordinary source blue and red edge strokes are rendered in black, preserving dashed visibility.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC; congruent parallel triangular ends ABC and DEF; longitudinal edges AD, BE and CF.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied vertex labels and equal-side ticks are visible; no calculated altitude or dimensions are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If $AB=8\text{ cm}$ and $BC=12\text{ cm}$, find the height of $\triangle ABC$, correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Since $AB=AC$, the altitude $AM$ bisects $BC$, so $BM=6\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}AM^2&=AB^2-BM^2\\AM^2&=8^2-6^2\\AM^2&=28\\AM&=\sqrt{28}\\AM&\approx5.29\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $AD=24\text{ cm}$, find the volume of the prism, correct to two decimal places.

answer.short:
$761.98\text{ cm}^3$

Multiply the triangular cross-sectional area by the prism length, retaining the exact height from part a.
answer.worked:
Using the exact triangular height $\sqrt{28}\text{ cm}$ from part a:

$$\begin{align*}V&=Ah\\V&=\left(\frac12\times12\times\sqrt{28}\right)\times24\\V&=288\sqrt7\\V&\approx761.98\text{ cm}^3.\end{align*}$$
